title: Sable Tech - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff to align onboarding milestones for Sable Tech's Redwood Private deployment. Covered integration options (VPC vs private), SSO/KMS requirements, pilot scope, success criteria, and initial timeline. Agreed to a security deep dive and to share onboarding playbook, SSO guide, and test dataset.

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Michael Rivera (Sable Tech Head of DevOps), Anya Singh (Platform Engineer), Liam O'Connor (Product)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align on Private deployment requirements, timeline for a 4-week pilot, and security/compliance asks. Recording quality: background noise on customer's side, some words garbled (medium).

[00:00] Maya Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, I know it's Friday afternoon, we'll go through the high level plan for onboarding Sable Tech onto Redwood Private and then hand over to Ethan for the technical bits. quick intro round?
[00:28] Michael Rivera: Yeah hi Michael here, head of devops at Sable, I'm the main infra point for this project.
[00:36] Anya Singh: Anya, platform infra, I'll be doing the VPC peering and network config.
[00:41] Liam O'Connor: Liam, product owner, I'll define success metrics and pilot users.
[00:45] Jordan Lee: Jordan from Redwood, I'm your AE, happy to help unblock contracts/attachments.
[00:50] Maya Ortiz: Cool, thanks. Quick agenda: timeline and milestones, deployment options (Private vs Dedicated), networking and KMS, SSO and RBAC, pilot scope, then next steps.
[01:10] Maya Ortiz: Our target is a 4-week pilot once the infra is ready, that typically includes integration, smoke tests, and a small production-like workload to validate latency and cost.
[01:28] Michael Rivera: Four weeks is fine, our constraint is we need isolated compute — can't send traffic outside our VPC. so Private deployment with a customer-managed control plane is non-negotiable.
[01:40] Ethan Chen: Understood. For Private we provide a control-plane option that either runs in your VPC or we provide an air-gapped package. Most customers do VPC peering and a private control plane. there are a couple of networking patterns we recommend.
[01:58] Anya Singh: Can you outline the networking patterns? we currently have strict egress policies and need to know firewall ports and endpoints.
[02:07] Ethan Chen: Yeah, so there are two common patterns: VPC peering where our control plane sits in a shared management VPC and we peer, or an on-prem package where the control plane is customer-hosted. Peering needs TCP 443 outbound to the management endpoints and inbound rules for the console, plus a few ephemeral ports for the agent. i'll share the exact firewall list after the call. Apologies if i mumble some of the ports, i've got that in a doc.
[02:36] Maya Ortiz: Note: we'll attach the networking checklist and the VPC template in the playbook.
[02:42] Liam O'Connor: Also, latency SLAs — we want sub-200ms tail latency for the demo queries; is that achievable on private?
[02:51] Ethan Chen: Sub-200ms is doable depending on model and instance type. for smaller models and proper KV cache/ prefix caching it'll be fine. if you need larger LLMs we'll need to size GPUs accordingly. we'll run a bench with your sample prompts.
[03:09] Michael Rivera: We also need to encrypt keys with our HSM — KMS integration is required. we use HashiCorp Vault backed KMS.
[03:18] Ethan Chen: We support KMS integrations; typically we integrate with AWS KMS or customer-managed vaults via an HSM abstraction. there might be an extra compliance review but it's supported. i'll log that as an action.
[03:32] Maya Ortiz: On SSO, do you use SAML/Okta or are you on Azure AD?
[03:38] Michael Rivera: Okta for employees, but some service accounts are on Azure. We want RBAC aligned to our AD groups.
[03:45] Ethan Chen: Okta works. we'll provide a SAML guide and a mapping template for roles to groups. small note, sometimes the emails come through weird in the auto-provisioning, so expect a short checklist.
[03:58] Maya Ortiz: Great. On success criteria, Liam, what are you tracking?
[04:04] Liam O'Connor: We want 1) integration completed with SSO and KMS, 2) pilot workload run with acceptable latency and no PII leakage, 3) cost estimation for production. if all three look good we want to expand to 1000 daily queries.
[04:20] Maya Ortiz: Solid. We'll add those as pilot success metrics in the playbook.
[04:27] Jordan Lee: On commercial side, i'm confirming the committed capacity contract options and trial credits. i'll follow up via email with the commitment options and pricing sheet.
[04:38] Michael Rivera: Cool. Also, compliance docs: SOC 2 and data residency, we need to share them with our security team.
[04:45] Maya Ortiz: Yes, we'll attach SOC 2 Type II, ISO and our data handling whitepaper. Expect those in the security bundle.
[04:52] Ethan Chen: Back on infra, a couple of gotchas from other customers: 1) KV cache priming — you'll want to pre-warm with common prompts, 2) batching settings affect tail latency, so we'll tune after bench results.
[05:10] Anya Singh: For the KV cache priming, do you need us to provide a seed set of prompts?
[05:15] Ethan Chen: Yeah, a 500-1,000 prompt sample set is ideal to simulate your traffic profile. we'll use that for the bench.
[05:22] Maya Ortiz: Action item — Ethan will share the test dataset template.
[05:26] Ethan Chen: I'll send that after the call.
[05:30] [small cross talk]
[06:00] Liam O'Connor: For telemetry, we want token-level cost estimates, per-route latency, and error rates. Does the console expose that by default?
[06:09] Ethan Chen: Yes, Redwood Console has token cost breakdown, per-model route dashboards, and traces. we'll enable an initial retention window; longer retention is an add-on.
[06:19] Maya Ortiz: We'll also include a sample dashboard config in the playbook so you can plug in your metrics tooling.
[06:25] Michael Rivera: On the legal side, is there a data processing agreement template we can start with?
[06:31] Jordan Lee: Yep i can circulate the DPA and the standard addendum; if you need custom terms we can loop legal once we have the pilot scoped.
[06:40] Anya Singh: Does Redwood support private model hosting or only open models? We have a licensed model that we may want to serve.
[06:48] Ethan Chen: For Private, you can bring-your-own-model. we support loading customer models, but we may need to adapt the runtime for quantization and perf. that's a separate onboarding track but doable.
[07:00] Liam O'Connor: Great. What's the expected infra footprint for an initial pilot of 2 QPS with latency target sub-200ms?
[07:08] Ethan Chen: For 2 QPS with small-medium model and caching, a single A100/ H100-equivalent instance in a dedicated pod should be sufficient for the pilot. we'll fine tune after benching.
[07:21] Maya Ortiz: Let's move to timeline. Proposed: Week 1 - infra & SSO setup, Week 2 - KMS + bench prep, Week 3 - pilot run & tuning, Week 4 - results and expansion decision. Any conflicts with that?
[07:38] Michael Rivera: That works on our side. Anya needs two business days to provision peering requests but timeline is acceptable.
[07:47] Anya Singh: Yes I can have peering ready by end of week 1 if i get the template.
[07:52] Maya Ortiz: We'll prioritize sending the VPC template and firewall list today.
[07:57] [08:30] Ethan Chen: Quick note: when we do the bench we'll collect a perf deck with p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost per 1K tokens. that helps you estimate monthly cost.
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: For cost estimates, do you include tokenization differences across models?
[08:51] Ethan Chen: We report tokens processed and estimate cost based on the model selected — different models will have different tokenization overheads, yes.
[09:00] Maya Ortiz: Security deep dive — Michael, who from your security team should join?
[09:07] Michael Rivera: i'll invite our security architect, Priya Raman, and legal counsel if needed. we'll aim for next week Tuesday or Wednesday.
[09:15] Maya Ortiz: I'll propose times for the week of March 9th.
[09:20] Jordan Lee: On procurement, i'll send contract templates and the DPA; if there's anything in procurement that blocks go-live, flag it early.
[09:29] Michael Rivera: noted. we typically have a two week legal review.
[09:34] Anya Singh: Are there logs we can ship to our SIEM? we'd like structured audit logs.
[09:40] Ethan Chen: Yes we provide audit logs and event streams. forwarding to your SIEM via secure delivery is supported. there may be a retention config and an add-on depending on the volume.
[09:54] Maya Ortiz: Ok let's recap action items — Ethan you'll share the bench and test dataset template, Maya you'll send playbook and SSO doc, Jordan will send contract and DPA, customer will provide network diagram and identify pilot users.
[10:10] Ethan Chen: I'll also include a troubleshooting doc for common network issues — sometimes the agent can't establish outbound TLS due to deep packet inspection.
[10:22] Michael Rivera: Good to know.
[10:26] Liam O'Connor: Pilot user list — we'll share names and roles by Monday.
[10:30] Anya Singh: I'll open the peering ticket as soon as i get the template.
[10:35] [11:00] Maya Ortiz: Any other questions or concerns?
[11:05] Michael Rivera: Not from me. just to reiterate KMS and SOC2 are blockers until they're cleared.
[11:12] Maya Ortiz: Understood. we'll prioritize security docs and the KMS integration plan.
[11:18] Jordan Lee: i'll follow up with the commercial paperwork and trial credits within 24 hours.
[11:24] Ethan Chen: i'll send the bench checklist and a sample perf deck today.
[11:30] Maya Ortiz: Great. Thanks everyone. we'll send notes and the playbook after the call and propose the security deep dive time.
[11:40] [11:50] Meeting ended.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-attributed speaker lines and small garbles around port numbers. The tech details will be confirmed in written docs attached to the playbook.

Attachments/References:
- Onboarding playbook (link to shared drive) - will be sent by Maya
- Network checklist and VPC template - to be shared
- SSO/SAML mapping guide - to be shared
- Benchmark checklist and perf deck sample - to be shared by Ethan
